name: Simple Contact Form – Accessible & Anti-Spam
author: Olaf Lederer

sections.description:
Most WordPress websites only need a simple contact form. You shouldn’t have to use a complex form builder just to receive a message from your website.

Simple Contact Form makes it easy to add an accessible contact form to your WordPress website in minutes. It includes effective built-in spam protection and works without complicated setup or unnecessary features.

Everything you need for a regular contact form is included for free. There is no premium version and no paid extensions.

Add your contact form using the block editor or a shortcode and you’re ready to receive messages.

Why use Simple Contact Form?

Easy to use

Create and add a contact form to your website in minutes, without learning how to use a complex form builder.

Accessible by default

Accessibility is built into your contact form, with proper labels, keyboard support and accessible validation.

Effective spam protection

Multiple built-in spam checks help stop unwanted messages without making it harder for real visitors to contact you.

Never lose a contact request

Contact form submissions can be stored in WordPress, so you’re not relying on email delivery alone.

Lightweight by design

CSS and JavaScript are only loaded on pages that contain a contact form, keeping unnecessary assets away from the rest of your website.

Ready to add a simple contact form to your website? Install Simple Contact Form and have your first contact form running in minutes.

What’s behind a simple contact form?

Curious about what makes Simple Contact Form work? Here’s a little secret: behind the scenes, it isn’t quite as simple as the name suggests.

The plugin and the way it handles contact form submissions are based on years of building websites for clients and testing different ways to keep contact form spam out. Many of the features below exist because they solved real problems on real websites.

You don’t need to understand or configure most of them to create a contact form. But if you want to know what’s happening behind the scenes, here’s what Simple Contact Form takes care of for you.

Accessibility

Your contact form should be easy to use for everyone. Accessibility is built into Simple Contact Form by default, so you don’t have to configure it separately.

  • Accessible form structure – Contact forms use proper labels and accessible HTML markup.
  • Accessible validation – Clear validation and error messages help visitors complete the form correctly.
  • Keyboard friendly – Visitors can complete and submit the contact form without using a mouse.
  • Works without JavaScript – The contact form remains functional when JavaScript is unavailable.

Anti-spam

Spam protection shouldn’t make it harder for real visitors to contact you. Simple Contact Form uses several built-in checks that work quietly in the background.

  • Invisible spam protection – Multiple checks help identify automated submissions without requiring visitors to solve a CAPTCHA.
  • Honeypot protection – Hidden fields help detect bots without affecting normal visitors.
  • Submission checks – Additional checks help distinguish genuine contact form submissions from automated spam.
  • Spam log – See what was blocked, why it was blocked and which spam checks are most effective.
  • Optional extra protection – Add Cloudflare Turnstile or WP Armour when additional protection is needed.

Good spam protection isn’t just about blocking spam.

An anti-spam solution can also block legitimate contact requests. Most website owners only discover this when someone reaches out another way to say their message didn’t get through — and you’ll never know how many others simply gave up.

That’s why Simple Contact Form keeps a spam log. It lets you see what was blocked and why, so you can check for false positives and adjust your spam protection when needed.

Easy to use

Simple Contact Form is made for contact forms, not for building complex applications. The plugin keeps setup and day-to-day management straightforward.

  • Quick setup – Create and publish a contact form without working through pages of settings.
  • Block or shortcode – Add your contact form with the block editor or use a shortcode wherever you need it.
  • Email notifications – Receive submitted contact messages directly by email.
  • Professional responder emails – Create and format HTML confirmation emails using the familiar WordPress editor.
  • Stored submissions – Keep contact form submissions in WordPress so messages aren’t only available by email.

Integrations & advanced options

Need a little more? Simple Contact Form includes optional integrations and advanced features without making them part of the basic setup.

  • Cloudflare Turnstile and WP Armour – Add additional anti-spam protection when needed.
  • Maileroo – Verify email addresses before accepting contact form submissions.
  • Country blocking – Use Country.is to block contact form submissions from selected countries.
  • Tracking options – Track successful contact form submissions when you need conversion data.
  • Developer friendly – Hooks are available for developers who want to customize or extend the contact form.
sections.installation:
The quickest method for installing the contact form is:

  1. Install the plugin using the built-in WordPress plugin installer, or upload the entire fws-ajax-contact-form folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ menu in WordPress.
  3. Open Contact form > Settings and configure the required options.
  4. Create a form and add it to a page using the block editor or the shortcode [fws_contact_form id="X"], where X is the ID of the form.
  5. Optionally create a responder email and select it in the form settings.

Visit our website for additional information.
sections.faq:
Does the contact form work without JavaScript?

That depends on the selected submission method.

The “AJAX with a non-JavaScript fallback” mode submits the form using AJAX when JavaScript is available. Without JavaScript, the form is submitted through the regular WordPress form handler.

The “AJAX only – JavaScript required” mode does not accept submissions without JavaScript.

What is the difference between the accessible challenge and Cloudflare Turnstile?

The accessible challenge is generated by the plugin and does not require an external service or JavaScript.

Cloudflare Turnstile is an optional external spam protection service. It requires JavaScript in the visitor’s browser and valid Turnstile site and secret keys.

When the non-JavaScript fallback is enabled, an accessible challenge can be used to protect submissions made without JavaScript.

Which information is shared with external services?

External requests are only made when the corresponding option is enabled.

Country.is receives the visitor’s IP address when country blocking is configured. Maileroo receives the submitted email address when email verification is enabled. Cloudflare receives the Turnstile verification data when Turnstile is configured.

What is the difference between Maileroo email verification and the Maileroo SMTP plugin?

Maileroo email verification checks whether a submitted email address can be accepted. The Maileroo SMTP plugin is a separate plugin that can deliver WordPress emails through Maileroo. Either feature can be used independently.

What should I do when the spam log file cannot be created?

The plugin uses standard file permissions for its spam log. If your hosting environment requires different permissions, ask your hosting provider which file permission should be used.

You can define FWSACF_CHMOD_FILE in wp-config.php using the value recommended by your hosting provider.

How to add a manual goal in Clicky?

If you use a Clicky premium plan it’s possible to track Goals.

  1. In Clicky, go to Goals > Setup > Create a new goal.
  2. Enter a name for the goal
  3. Check the “Manual Goal” checkbox and click Submit
  4. Copy/paste the ID into the field from the plugin options page

How to use the “fwsacf_after_success_form” action hook?

Use the following action hook in your theme’s function.php file. For example you can submit the email address and name to your CRM or email marketing system to send out some follow up emails.

    add_action('fwsacf_after_success_form', function($form) {
            // Your code here...
            // and use the array values $form['email'] and $form['name'] where needed
        });

How to use the dynamic subject feature?

Using this feature is easy, just add the subject text as query string to the page URL where your contact form is located, for example: https://domain.com/contact/?dynsubject=yourtexthere

How can I report security bugs?

You can report security bugs through the Patchstack Vulnerability Disclosure Program. The Patchstack team help validate, triage and handle any security vulnerabilities. Report a security vulnerability.
sections.changelog:
1.6.1

  • Enhancement
    • Added an option to remove all plugin settings and stored data during uninstall. Plugin data is preserved by default.
  • Other
    • Changed the name from Ajax Conact Form into Simple Contact Form

1.6.0

  • Enhancements

    • Added a choice between AJAX submission with a non-JavaScript fallback and AJAX-only submission.
    • Rebuilt the form processing flow using separate classes for requests, validation, spam protection, submissions and email delivery.
    • Rebuilt the administration code for forms, responders, submissions, settings and spam logs.
    • Improved the order and separation of spam checks.
    • Improved the integration between Cloudflare Turnstile and the accessible form challenge.
    • Improved required-field validation for optional form fields.
    • Added structured error codes for failed validation and spam checks.
    • Improved the spam log dashboard and added a protected log download.
    • Added logging for submissions blocked by country.
    • Improved the HTML templates for administrator and responder emails.
    • Added a mail transport interface to support future email delivery integrations.
    • Improved support for multiple recipients, responder Bcc addresses and custom mail headers.
    • Improved the settings page and tab navigation.
    • Improved the form, responder and submission management screens.

  • Bug fixes

    • Fixed header warnings caused by setting the form load-time cookie too late.
    • Fixed missing form configuration values for the challenge and optional fields.
    • Fixed administrator emails being sent without the HTML email template.
    • Fixed several missing or duplicated components left over from the procedural implementation.
    • Fixed translation loading being triggered before the WordPress init action.
    • Fixed settings fields not being displayed or saved correctly.
    • Fixed validation and display of responder email fields.
    • Fixed the spam log file permission handling.

  • Other

    • Removed the hCaptcha integration.
    • Refactored most procedural plugin code into reusable and testable classes.
